_meta.description: Module function guide — Contains descriptions and parameter details for each function. Changes take effect without server restart.

PCAN._description: PCAN (python-can) — Connects to CAN interfaces such as PCAN/Vector/Kvaser via python-can to send CAN/CAN FD messages and save CSV logs. Register one device per hardware unit and select the channel via each step's channel argument. Connection lifecycle is managed automatically by the scenario.

send_can.description: Sends a single CAN/CAN FD frame on the given channel.

params.msg_id: CAN message ID (hex). e.g. '0x621' or '621' (both mean 0x621).
params.data: Data bytes (space- or comma-separated hex). e.g. '45 40 FF FF FF FF FF FF'
params.is_fd: Send this frame as CAN FD? True/False (auto FD if the bus is in FD mode).
params.brs: FD Bit Rate Switch. Leave empty to auto-enable on FD frames (matches the reference sender; standard for 500k/2M buses). Always OFF for classic frames.

send_periodic_can.description: Starts or updates a cyclic (periodic) send on the given channel. Calling again with the same channel+ID only updates the data. Stop with stop_all_tx or can_all_stop.

params.data: Data bytes (space/comma-separated hex). e.g. '45 40 FF FF FF FF FF FF'
params.period_ms: Send period in milliseconds. e.g. '500'. Default 1000.
params.brs: FD Bit Rate Switch. Leave empty to auto-enable on FD frames (matches the reference sender; standard for 500k/2M buses). Always OFF for classic frames.

stop_all_tx.description: Stops all running cyclic (periodic) send tasks across all channels.

start_logging.description: Starts logging CAN traffic from all open channels into a single CSV file (Timestamp,Message_id,Dir,DLC,Data,channel — the channel column distinguishes channels).

params.csv_file: CSV path to save. If empty, auto-saved under the playback run folder (logs/) or results/PCAN_Log.

stop_logging.description: Stops CSV logging and saves the file (flush+close).

can_all_stop.description: Stops all periodic sends and logging across all channels at once (connection kept alive).

check_status.description: Diagnostics: reports the channel's bus state (ok/error/bus-off) and the number of open channels & periodic tasks. Use to narrow down why sends aren't working (channel/bitrate vs ID/data/wakeup).

CANAT._description: CANat Device — Sends and receives CAN bus messages via CANat hardware

init.description: Initializes and connects the CANat device.

params.ch1_fd: Channel 1 CAN FD mode. True (default) = FD, False = Classic
params.ch2_fd: Channel 2 CAN FD mode. True = FD, False (default) = Classic

CAN_PANEL.description: Reaction-time visualization panel for CAN. With state=On and no signal it shows a black panel and waits; with state=On and a signal (message_id + can_message) it flashes the panel yellow while simultaneously sending send_can_message with no delay (film the panel with a camera and count frames from the yellow flash to the on-screen reaction to measure latency); with state=OFF it resets the panel to black only if it is already open (does nothing if not open — never spawns a new window); with state=Close it closes the panel.

params.state: Panel state. 'On' (show/flash+send), 'OFF' (reset to black only if already open, no spawn), 'Close' (close panel)
params.message_id: CAN message ID. When state=on and both this and can_message are set, it sends + flashes (black panel only if either is empty)
params.x: Panel top-left X (px). Empty = bottom-left default. Auto-filled by the 'Crop monitor' button
params.y: Panel top-left Y (px). Empty = bottom-left default

check_can_message.description: Checks whether a specific CAN message is received (RX) within the timeout. PASS if received, FAIL otherwise. Leave data empty to check message ID reception only. Works as a single step — no prepare/cleanup steps needed.

params.message_id: CAN message ID to check (hex). e.g. '0x18DAF141' or '291'
params.expected_data: Expected data (hex bytes, space-separated). Empty = ID-only check. '*' ignores a nibble — e.g. '1A 2B', '1* ** 33'

match_mode.description: Data comparison mode. 'startswith' (default: prefix match) / 'exact' (full-length match) / 'contains' (match anywhere in data) / 'bitmask' (all set bits present)

params.timeout: Max wait time in seconds (default 5). Returns PASS immediately when matched

check_no_can_message.description: Inverse check — PASS only if the message is NOT received during the timeout. Fails immediately on first reception (e.g. a message must stop after entering sleep).

params.message_id: CAN message ID that must not be received (hex). e.g. '0x18DAF141'
params.expected_data: Expected data (hex bytes). Empty = any reception of the ID fails. '*' nibble wildcard supported
params.timeout: Watch duration in seconds (default 5). PASS if not received for this long

stop_can_message.description: Stops periodic transmission of a specific CAN message.

can_message_save_start.description: Starts saving CAN messages to a file.

params.save_path: Save path. Uses default path if empty

CANoe_RBS._description: CANoe RBS control (py_canoe/COM) — Drives the CANoe application via COM to start/stop cfg (RBS)-based measurement, control signals and system/environment variables, and run UDS diagnostics.

Init_CANoe_Plugin.description: Initializes CANoe and opens the cfg (kills existing CANoe processes, clears the win32com gen_py cache, initializes COM). Call this first before measurement/diagnostics.

params.canoe_log_dir: py_canoe log folder. Default '.\Log' (a timestamped subfolder is created automatically)

Quit.description: Quits CANoe (force-kills the process on failure).

SendSignal.description: Sets a signal value of a message.

GetSignal.description: Reads a signal value (returns only values received during measurement; otherwise errors).

GetSysVar.description: Reads a system variable value (falls back to raw COM to surface the real cause when py_canoe returns None).

return_symbolic_name.description: Whether to return the symbolic name. Default False

islog.description: Whether to print a log. Default True

CheckSysVar.description: Compares a system variable value against an expected value (pass/fail).

GetEnvVar.description: Reads an environment variable value (use GetSysVar if it's a System Variables namespace variable).

islog.description: Whether to print a log. Default True

CheckEnvVar.description: Compares an environment variable value against an expected value (pass/fail).

DIAG_TestPresent.description: Turns periodic Tester Present transmission on or off for the given ECU.

DIAG_Request.description: Sends a UDS diagnostic request and returns the response.

request_in_bytes.description: Interpret request as bytes. Default True

return_sender_name.description: Include sender name in the response. Default False

islog.description: Whether to print a log. Default True

CheckDIAG.description: Sends a UDS diagnostic request and compares the response against an expected pattern (supports indexed comparison).

request_in_bytes.description: Interpret request as bytes. Default True

return_sender_name.description: Include sender name in the response. Default False

SendDiagMsg.description: Sends a UDS diagnostic request, parses PRC/NRC, and returns a dict (retries on timeout).

request_in_bytes.description: Interpret request as bytes. Default True

return_sender_name.description: Include sender name in the response. Default False

params.max_retries: Maximum number of retries on timeout. Default 5

CANoe_Ctrl._description: CANoe direct control (Vector) — Sends/receives CAN/CAN FD messages, saves ASC logs, and runs ISO-TP (UDS) diagnostics via Vector CAN hardware (python-can VectorBus). No CANoe application required.

canoe_full_log_save_start.description: Starts saving all CAN traffic to an ASC log file (receives from all bus channels). Returns the final timestamped save path.

params.file_name: Log file name (with extension). e.g. 'Auto.asc' — '_YYMMDD_HHMMSS' is appended automatically.

canoe_full_log_save_stop.description: Stops full log saving and cleans up periodic transmit tasks.

canoe_log_save_start.description: Starts a section log (saves an additional section to a separate file while full logging is active).

canoe_send_message.description: Sends a CAN/CAN FD message. A non-zero cycle time sends periodically; 0 sends once. When apply_e2e=True, the Alive Counter and CRC16 are recomputed in real time every cycle for an E2E-protected periodic transmit.

params.bus_channel: Bus channel index (from 0, in device_info order)
params.message_type: 'FD' (default) or any other string = Classic CAN

apply_e2e.description: True = E2E (Alive Counter + CRC16) periodic transmit; False (default) = plain transmit. E2E spec is read per message_id from plugins/e2e_config.json, falling back to a default template. Only effective when cycle_time > 0.

canoe_send_message_stop.description: Stops the periodic transmit of a single CAN ID (both E2E and plain periodic). Other periodic messages keep running.

params.message_id: CAN ID to stop (hex string). e.g. '0xA0'

canoe_send_msg_all_stop.description: Stops all periodic transmits on the given channel (including E2E).

load_e2e_config.description: Reloads the E2E spec JSON file. Defaults to plugins/e2e_config.json when omitted. (Auto-loaded once at module init; call only to re-apply after editing the file.)

params.config_path: Path to the E2E config JSON. Leave empty to use the default file (plugins/e2e_config.json).

find_msg_from_latest_log.description: Searches a log file for a line containing a specific CAN ID and data. Returns ('pass', line) or ('fail', '').

params.log_file: Path of the log file to search
params.can_message: Data to check for inclusion (space-separated hex)

canoe_set_diag_env.description: Configures the ISO-TP (diagnostic) environment. Must be called once before sending/receiving diagnostics.

params.bus_ch: Bus channel index used for diagnostics

canoe_start_tester_present.description: Starts sending periodic Tester Present (3E 00) messages (keeps the diagnostic session alive).

canoe_stop_tester_present.description: Stops sending periodic Tester Present messages.

canoe_send_diag_msg.description: Sends a diagnostic (UDS) message via ISO-TP and evaluates the response (PRC/NRC). Returns a dict with status/response/service_id, etc. (requires canoe_set_diag_env first)

params.can_message: Diagnostic data to send (space-separated hex). e.g. '22 F1 90'

wait_response.description: Whether to wait for and evaluate the response. Default True

SSHManager._description: SSH Connection — Connects to remote devices via SSH for command execution and file transfer

params.hostname: Remote device IP or hostname. e.g. '192.168.1.100'
params.key_filePath: SSH key file path (alternative to password). Default: None

send_command.description: Executes a command via SSH and returns the full output on completion (blocking). Korean Windows output is automatically handled via cp949/euc-kr encoding. Writing the command as 'bash -s < <local path>' auto-injects that local (PC) file as stdin, running a local script remotely without uploading.

params.command: Command to execute. e.g. 'ls -al', 'cat /etc/version'. Writing it as 'bash -s < <local path>' auto-injects that local (PC) file as stdin so a local script runs remotely without uploading. e.g. 'sudo bash -s < C:\ReplayKit\scripts\Check_Battery.sh'. During playback, {cycle} (current repeat index) and {timestamp} (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS) are substituted — e.g. 'slog2info -w all > /var/qnx_slog_{cycle}_{timestamp}.txt &'

send_command_stream.description: Executes a command via SSH and immediately returns a [BG_TASK:bg_x] placeholder (non-blocking). Output streams in real time and can be observed via the polling endpoint. Useful for long-running commands (netstat, tail -f, etc.).

Check.description: Executes a command via SSH and compares the output against an expected value (blocking). Returns a 'FAIL:' prefix on failure so the step is judged as failed. Korean output is automatically handled via cp949/euc-kr encoding. Writing the command as 'bash -s < <local path>' auto-injects that local (PC) file as stdin, running a local script remotely without uploading.

params.command: Command to execute. Writing it as 'bash -s < <local path>' auto-injects that local (PC) file as stdin so a local script runs remotely without uploading. e.g. 'sudo bash -s < C:\ReplayKit\scripts\Check_Battery.sh'
params.expected: Expected string that must be contained in or exactly match the output. Leave empty for 'pass only when there is no output' (no-output check)
params.match_mode: Comparison mode: 'contains' (substring) or 'exact' (full match). Default: contains

Check_Logic.description: Executes a command via SSH and judges pass/fail against multiple keywords using and/or logic (blocking). Returns a 'FAIL:' prefix on failure so the step is judged as failed. Writing the command as 'bash -s < <local path>' auto-injects that local (PC) file as stdin, running a local script remotely without uploading.

params.command: Command to execute. Writing it as 'bash -s < <local path>' auto-injects that local (PC) file as stdin so a local script runs remotely without uploading. e.g. 'sudo bash -s < C:\ReplayKit\scripts\Check_Battery.sh'
params.logic: Logic: 'and' (pass when all keywords present) or 'or' (pass when at least one present). Default: and

send_file.description: Transfers a local file to the remote device.

get_file.description: Downloads a file from the remote device to the PC.

get_folder.description: Recursively downloads an entire folder (including subfolders) from the remote device to the PC via SFTP. Non-regular files such as symlinks are skipped. If some files fail, returns a 'FAIL:' prefix so the step is judged as fail.

params.remote_path: Folder path on remote device. e.g. '/var/log'
params.local_path: Destination folder path on PC. If empty during playback, saved automatically under the run folder's logs/ with the remote folder name. If a folder with the same name already has content, it is NOT overwritten — '_2', '_3' … is appended instead (keeps each run separate)

get_file_list_in_dir.description: Lists files in a directory on the remote device.

DLTLogging._description: DLT Logging — Captures and saves logs via direct TCP connection to the DLT daemon, with keyword-based PASS/FAIL evaluation (no GUI required)

StartLogging.description: Connects to DLT and starts capture. Streams all logs immediately to a text file (auto path) while keeping only recent entries in memory (stays fast even for long runs). A raw .dlt file (same path, .dlt extension) is written in parallel so the capture can be reopened in DLT Viewer. The viewer modal opens automatically.

StopLogging.description: Stops DLT capture. Logs are already saved to file in real time; specifying save_path only moves the file to that location. The raw .dlt file is moved alongside it (same path, .dlt extension).

params.save_path: Save file path. If empty, keeps the streaming files as-is (during replay: run_dir/logs/dlt/c{cycle}_dlt_*.log + .dlt, step test: backend/results/Temp_logs/). Supports {cycle}/{timestamp} variables

WaitLog.description: Waits (blocking) until a log containing the keyword appears. Returns FAIL on timeout.

ExpectFound.description: Periodically searches the entire log until the keyword is found. Searches immediately, then retries at intervals (timeout / max_retries). Returns PASS if found, FAIL if not found after all retries.

params.max_retries: Maximum retry count (default: 5). Interval = timeout / max_retries

ExpectNotFound.description: Periodically checks the entire log to confirm the keyword is absent. Returns FAIL immediately if found. Rechecks at intervals (timeout / max_retries). Returns PASS if not found after all checks.

params.max_retries: Maximum check count (default: 5). Interval = timeout / max_retries

SerialLogging._description:
Serial Logging — Captures serial port logs with keyword-based fail detection.

**Connection lifecycle**: The serial port itself is opened/closed by the Device tab's Connect/Disconnect. StartLogging does NOT reopen an already-open port, so devices that reset their settings on every connect are safe.

**⚠️ Usage: StartLogging and StopLogging are paired.**
- Without StopLogging the memory buffer is never written to a file.
- StopLogging ends the capture session but **keeps the serial port open**. To close the port, use the Device tab Disconnect.
- On abnormal scenario exit, cleanup auto-saves any unsaved buffer during Disconnect.

Standard usage pattern:
  1) StartLogging()                              ← first step (capture starts; port pre-opened via Device tab Connect)
  2) SendCommand / SendCommand_*_on_keyword ...  ← middle steps
  3) StopLogging()                               ← last step (writes log file + ends capture, port stays open)

StartLogging.description:
Starts serial capture (memory only, no file save). Viewer modal opens automatically. **If the port is already open, no reconnect happens** — only the capture session is (re)started, so devices that reset on connect are safe. Returns once the capture thread is ready, so the next step's SendCommand is not dropped.

**⚠️ Must be paired with StopLogging.** Without StopLogging the in-memory buffer is never flushed to disk.

params.settle_ms: Port stabilization wait after open (ms). Default 500. **Skipped if the port is already open.** Used only on the first open to ensure USB-Serial driver reset/buffer settle. Use 1500~2000 for DTR-reset boards (Arduino).

StopLogging.description:
Writes the memory buffer to a file and ends the capture session. **The serial port is kept open** — subsequent SendCommand calls will not re-initialize the device. To close the port, use the Device tab Disconnect.

**⚠️ Must be paired with StartLogging.** This call is what:
  • Flushes the in-memory log buffer to a .log file on disk
  • Tears down the capture thread to avoid resource leaks
  • Allows the next StartLogging to begin a fresh session
Even if the file-save step throws, the finally block guarantees the capture is torn down.

params.save_path: Save file path. Auto if empty (during playback: run_dir/logs/serial/c{cycle}_serial_{port}_*.log, step test: backend/results/Temp_logs/serial_*.log). Supports {cycle}/{timestamp} variables

SendCommand.description: Sends a text command via the serial port.

params.command: Command to send. e.g. 'reboot', 'cat /proc/version'. During playback, {cycle}/{timestamp} variables are substituted

Send_Packet.description: Sends a raw hex byte packet over the serial port. Each space-separated hex token is converted to a single byte and sent, then flushed to guarantee it reaches the wire (1-digit / 2-digit / 0x-prefixed tokens are all accepted).

params.data: Space-separated hex string. e.g. '79 6D F2 0F' or '00 77 42 37 02 F2 00 FE'

SendCommand_fail_on_keyword.description: Sends a command, then **FAILS if the keyword appears** in the response. Used to detect abnormal keywords like 'ERROR'/'Fail'/'crash'. After sending, monitors only newly captured lines for 'time' seconds; every matching line is appended as a fail row and displayed inline (Fail_Count_N). Returns PASS if no match.

SendCommand_pass_on_keyword.description: Sends a command, then **PASSES if the keyword appears** in the response. Used for normal-response keywords like 'OK'/'Pass'/'BootComplete'. Returns PASS immediately on first match (early exit). If not found within 'time' seconds, appends one fail row and returns FAIL.

Monitor_pass_on_keyword.description: WITHOUT sending any command (no write), PASS if keyword is found in the log. If include_past=True, first scans logs captured so far, then monitors new lines for `time` seconds; PASS on first match. Sends nothing (not even a newline), so it does not disturb a webcam on the same USB hub.

params.time: Seconds to wait for future log lines. Default 5. 0 = scan past buffer only

include_past.description: Whether to also scan logs captured so far. true/false (default true)

Monitor_fail_on_keyword.description: WITHOUT sending any command (no write), FAIL if keyword is found in the log. For monitoring abnormal keywords (ERROR/crash). Scans past buffer (if include_past) and new lines for `time` seconds, accumulating all matches.

params.time: Seconds to monitor future log lines. Default 5. 0 = scan past buffer only

include_past.description: Whether to also scan logs captured so far. true/false (default true)

SmartBench._description: Smart Bench TCP Control — Controls power, buttons, current, and LEDs on Smart Bench equipment via TCP socket

Connect.description: Connects to the Smart Bench via TCP.

CheckCurrent.description: Measures current and returns PASS if within range for 3 consecutive readings, FAIL on timeout.

CheckCurrentMoment.description: Measures instantaneous current and returns PASS if within range, FAIL if out of range for 3 consecutive readings.

CheckCurrentMaintain.description: Verifies that current stays within range for the specified duration.

SendRaw.description: Sends a raw text command directly.

WoohyunBench._description: Woohyun Bench — Integrated UDP test bench: vehicle power control (IGN/ACC/Battery) + CAN FD signal transmission

Connect.description: Establishes a UDP network connection to the bench equipment. Automatically called when adding the device, so manual invocation is usually unnecessary.

Disconnect.description: Disconnects the UDP network connection from the bench equipment.

IsConnected.description: Checks whether the bench equipment is currently connected.

IGN1.description: Turns IGN1 (Ignition 1) power on or off. Corresponds to the vehicle's ignition power.

IGN1_Read.description: Reads the current IGN1 power state. Returns: 0=OFF, 1=ON, -1=read failure

IGN2.description: Turns IGN2 (Ignition 2) power on or off. Corresponds to auxiliary ignition power.

IGN2_Read.description: Reads the current IGN2 power state. Returns: 0=OFF, 1=ON, -1=read failure

ACC.description: Turns ACC (Accessory) power on or off. Corresponds to the vehicle's accessory power (radio, navigation, etc.).

ACC_Read.description: Reads the current ACC power state. Returns: 0=OFF, 1=ON, -1=read failure

BATTERY.description: Turns the battery relay on or off. When OFF, battery power is completely cut from the vehicle.

BATTERY_Read.description: Reads the current battery relay state. Returns: 0=OFF, 1=ON, -1=read failure

BatterySet.description: Sets the battery output voltage. Used for voltage fluctuation testing.

params.voltage: Voltage to set (V, decimal allowed). e.g. 12.0, 14.4, 9.0. Default: 14.4V

BatteryCheck.description: Measures the current battery output voltage. Returns: voltage (V), -1.0 on failure

AmpereCheck.description: Measures the current power consumption. Returns: current (A), -1.0 on failure

GetInfo.description: Returns the bench's current connection information (connected MCUs, signal_file, connection state).

LoadSignals.description: Loads CAN FD signal definitions from an Excel (.xls/.xlsx) or XML (.CAN) file at runtime.

params.file_path: Absolute path to the signal definition file

SendSignal.description: Sends a named CAN FD signal with the given physical value. Repeats 5 times at 200ms interval. Requires signal definitions to be loaded.

DoorTest.description: Cycles the driver door switch signal (Warn_DrvDrSwSta) ON/OFF to verify door handling.

TestAllSignals.description: Sends every loaded CAN FD signal with its midpoint value. Useful for load/sanity testing.

SendTimeSync.description: Broadcasts a time-sync packet over UDP to all bench equipment. Automatically called on Connect, so manual invocation is usually unnecessary.

canmsg_start.description: Starts pre-capturing CAN messages. Begins recording all received packets on every channel into a background ring buffer (up to 100k entries). Call this BEFORE the control step (e.g. IGN1) so that short one-shot responses fired right after the command are not missed. Verify afterwards with canmsg_stop.

canmsg_stop.description: Stops the CAN capture and verifies the buffer. Checks whether any packet captured since canmsg_start matches the target MCU/channel/msg_id/data pattern. Returns PASS on a match, or a 'FAIL:' string so the step is marked failed. Usage order: canmsg_start → control command → (wait) → canmsg_stop

mcu.description: Target MCU to listen on (default: 'mcu1' / e.g. 'mcu1', 'mcu2', 'mcu3')

params.msg_id: CAN ID to verify. Integer or hex string (with or without '0x'. e.g. '0x12F', '47A', 1146)
params.data: Data pattern to match. Hex bytes separated by spaces/commas. '*' or '**' positions are wildcards (ignored), and received bytes beyond the pattern length are not compared. e.g. '00 00 00 00 05 00 00 00' or '** ** ** ** 05'

canmsg.description: [Legacy compatibility] Verifies CAN message reception. Collects packets for the specified time (ms) starting at the moment of the call, then checks for a msg_id/data pattern match. One-shot responses that occur before the call cannot be caught, so use canmsg_start → control → canmsg_stop for new scenarios.

mcu.description: Target MCU to listen on (default: 'mcu1' / e.g. 'mcu1', 'mcu2', 'mcu3')

params.msg_id: CAN ID to verify. Integer or hex string (with or without '0x'. e.g. '0x12F', '47A', 1146)
params.data: Data pattern to match. Hex bytes separated by spaces/commas. '*' or '**' positions are wildcards (ignored), and received bytes beyond the pattern length are not compared. e.g. '00 00 00 00 05 00 00 00' or '** ** ** ** 05'

SendCan.description: Sends a raw CAN frame. Transmits a standard/extended/FD frame to the given device (mcu) and channel, either once or periodically.

params.msg_id: CAN ID. Integer or hex string (parsed as hex regardless of '0x' prefix. e.g. '0x33E', '47A')
params.payload_hex: Payload hex bytes (spaces/commas allowed, no brackets. e.g. '00,00,00,00,00,C0,00,00' or 'FF 01 02')
params.cycle_ms: Send interval in ms when repeat=1 (default: 200)

SendStopCan.description: Stops the periodic transmission of a specific Raw CAN message corresponding to the provided msg_id.

params.msg_id: Target CAN ID to stop (integer or hex string. Parsed as hex regardless of the '0x' prefix. e.g. '0x33E', '47A')

SendAllStopCan.description: Stops all active periodic Raw CAN message transmissions across all connected MCUs simultaneously.

CanSaveStart.description: Starts unified real-time logging of Rx/Tx CAN data from every connected MCU/channel into a single CSV file.

params.save_dir: CSV save folder path. Defaults to ./canlog when empty (filename CAN_LOG_<timestamp>.csv is auto-generated)

CanSaveStop.description: Stops unified CAN logging and closes the CSV file.

CMD._description: Command Execution — Executes Windows command prompt (CMD) commands. Used for running external programs or system commands

Run.description: Executes a command and waits for completion (blocking). Returns the result.

params.timeout: Max wait time in seconds. Default: 300

Check.description: Executes a command and verifies the output against an expected string (blocking). Returns a 'FAIL:' prefix on mismatch, which causes the step to be marked as fail.

params.expected: Expected substring or full match value
params.match_mode: Comparison mode: 'contains' (substring) or 'exact' (full match). Default: contains
params.timeout: Max wait time in seconds. Default: 300

Check_Logic.description: Executes a command and judges the output against multiple keywords with and/or logic (blocking). Returns a 'FAIL:' prefix on failure, which causes the step to be marked as fail.

params.logic: Judgement logic: 'and' (pass if all keywords are present) or 'or' (pass if at least one is present). Default: and
params.timeout: Max wait time in seconds. Default: 30

RunCapture.description: Executes a command in the background and immediately returns a '[BG_TASK:bg_x]' placeholder (non-blocking). The actual output can be retrieved later via the polling endpoint.

CheckCapture.description: Executes a command in the background and returns a '[BG_TASK:bg_x]' placeholder. On completion, the server evaluates expected/match_mode to determine the final pass/fail.

RunBackground.description: Spawns a subprocess fire-and-forget. Returns the PID but the output cannot be retrieved.

params.pid: PID of the process to terminate

ListBackground.description: Returns the list of running background processes.

SHELL._description: Shell Command Execution — Executes Linux/macOS bash commands. Linux counterpart of CMD. Used for running external programs or system commands.

Run.description: Executes a bash command and waits for completion (blocking). Returns the result.

params.command: bash command to execute. e.g. 'ls -la /tmp', 'ps -ef | grep python'
params.timeout: Max wait time in seconds. Default: 30

Check.description: Executes a bash command and verifies the output against an expected string (blocking). Returns a 'FAIL:' prefix on mismatch, which causes the step to be marked as fail.

params.expected: Expected substring or full-match value. Empty = pass only when output is empty (no-output check)
params.match_mode: Comparison mode: 'contains' (substring) or 'exact' (full match). Default: contains
params.timeout: Max wait time in seconds. Default: 30

Check_Logic.description: Executes a bash command and verifies the output against multiple keywords using and/or logic (blocking). Returns a 'FAIL:' prefix on mismatch.

params.logic: 'and' (all keywords required) or 'or' (any one). Default: and
params.timeout: Max wait time in seconds. Default: 30

RunCapture.description: Executes a command in the background and immediately returns a '[BG_TASK:bg_x]' placeholder (non-blocking).

CheckCapture.description: Executes a command in the background and returns a '[BG_TASK:bg_x]' placeholder. On completion, the server evaluates expected/match_mode for final pass/fail.

RunBackground.description: Spawns a bash subprocess fire-and-forget. Detaches via setsid so it survives caller termination. Returns the PID but output cannot be retrieved.

params.command: bash command to execute. e.g. 'sleep 60', 'python3 script.py'

params.pid: PID of the process to terminate

ListBackground.description: Returns the list of running background processes.

HKMC6th._description: HKMC 6th-gen IVI device — Screen capture / touch / swipe / HW key control over a TCP socket protocol. Calls the HKMC6thService functions of the connected hkmc_agent device directly.

params.screen_type: Screen type. front_center / rear_left / rear_right / cluster

repeat_tap.description: Taps the same coordinate N times in a row (for fast double/multi taps).

params.screen_type: Screen type. front_center / rear_left / rear_right / cluster

long_press.description: Presses the given coordinate, holds for duration_ms, then releases.

params.screen_type: Screen type. front_center / rear_left / rear_right / cluster
Screen type. front_center / rear_left / rear_right / cluster

send_key.description: Sends a HW key event (6th-gen keyExt6th packet). See the HKMC spec for cmd/sub_cmd/key_data values.

send_key_by_name.description: Sends a HW key event by key name (applies spec default + device override).

screencap.description: Captures the current screen and saves it to a file.

screencap_bytes.description: Captures the current screen and returns the bytes (BMP/PNG) without saving to a file.

params.screen_type: Screen type. front_center / rear_left / rear_right / cluster

get_screen_size.description: Returns the (width, height) size of the given screen.

params.screen_type: Screen type. front_center / rear_left / rear_right / cluster

execute_shell.description: Sends a shell command packet (low-level — specify cmd/sub_cmd/resp directly).

send_shell_cmd.description: Sends a simple shell string command to the device.

Check.description: Runs an ADB shell command and compares the output against an expected value for PASS/FAIL (same contract as Check in the CMD/SSH modules). The shell prefix is added automatically if missing. On mismatch, the 'FAIL:' prefix makes the step fail automatically.

params.command: Device shell command to run (e.g. getprop ro.build.version.release — shell prefix optional)
params.expected: Expected value. If empty, passes only when there is no output (no-output check)
params.match_mode: contains (substring match, default) or exact (full match)
params.serial: Target ADB device serial. Empty = derived from the step's device

Check_Logic.description: Runs an ADB shell command and judges multiple keywords with and/or logic (same contract as Check_Logic in the CMD/SSH modules). The shell prefix is added automatically if missing. On mismatch, the 'FAIL:' prefix makes the step fail automatically.

params.command: Device shell command to run (e.g. dumpsys activity — shell prefix optional)
params.logic: and (pass when all keywords present, default) or or (pass when at least one present)
params.serial: Target ADB device serial. Empty = derived from the step's device

StartLogging.description: Start capturing logcat for the given Android device (in-memory buffer). If clear=True, flushes the logcat ring buffer first. Auto-restarts logcat into the same buffer if the device reboots/disconnects.

params.serial: Target ADB device serial. Empty = derived from the step's device

clear.description: Clear logcat buffer before starting. true/false (default true)

StopLogging.description: Stop logcat capture and save the buffer to a file ({run_dir}/logs/logcat/c{cycle}_logcat_*.log during playback, results/Temp_logs/ for step tests).

params.serial: Target ADB device serial. Empty = derived from the step's device

ClearLog.description: Clear the device's logcat ring buffer (adb logcat -c).

params.serial: Target ADB device serial. Empty = derived from the step's device

Monitor_pass_on_keyword.description: PASS if keyword is found in the captured logcat. If include_past=True, scans logs captured so far first, then monitors new lines for `time` seconds. Requires StartLogging first.

params.time: Seconds to wait for future log lines. Default 5. 0 = past buffer only
params.serial: Target ADB device serial. Empty = derived from the step's device

include_past.description: Whether to also scan logs captured so far. true/false (default true)

Monitor_fail_on_keyword.description: FAIL if keyword is found in the captured logcat. For monitoring abnormal keywords (FATAL/ANR/Exception). Scans past buffer (if include_past) and new lines for `time` seconds.

params.time: Seconds to monitor future log lines. Default 5. 0 = past buffer only
params.serial: Target ADB device serial. Empty = derived from the step's device

include_past.description: Whether to also scan logs captured so far. true/false (default true)

Frame_Check._description: Operation-time measurement tool based on the test recording video (webcam). Add a Frame_Measure step to the scenario; when the scenario ends, webcam recording stops automatically and the video is analyzed frame by frame to report the elapsed time (ms) from the measurement start point to the first appearance of the target image, along with a clip of the measured section (5s before start to 5s after end). The PIP webcam must be open before playback for recording/measurement.

Frame_Measure.description: Defines one operation-time measurement. The start point is this step's execution time with mode='function', or the first frame where start_image appears (after execution) with mode='image'. The target is the first frame where target_image appears after start point + wait_time; if not found within max_time seconds it is reported as not found. Use the edit button to crop the current PIP webcam frame.

params.mode: Start-point basis: 'function' (step execution time) or 'image' (first frame start_image appears)
params.start_image: Start-point image (required when mode='image'). Set by cropping the webcam frame via the edit button
params.start_threshold: Start image match similarity threshold (0.0~1.0, default 0.8)
params.wait_time: Grace period in seconds before the target can appear. Target scanning skips this interval after the start point (default 0)
params.target_image: Target image (required). Set by cropping the webcam frame via the edit button
params.target_threshold: Target image match similarity threshold (0.0~1.0, default 0.8)
params.max_time: Maximum scan time in seconds from the scan start point. 0 = unlimited (default 60)
